newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas mostly lower despite cold.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas mostly lower despite cold.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were mostly lower Thursday despite cold temperatures in western Canada, sources said.
At the AECO storage hub, prices hovered in the C$2.32-2.35 per gigajoule (GJ) area, with the lower-priced deals reported done late.
These prices indicate only about a cent drop from Wednesday's levels.
Temperatures in Calgary dropped to about -20 degrees Celsius today, lending support to the domestic market.
Summer AECO prices were talked slightly higher around C$1.63 per GJ.

At Sumas, Wash., the western Canadian export point, prices dropped into the $3.05-3.10 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) range, as temperatures climbed to about five degrees Fahrenheit above-normal in the Pacific Northwest and hydro supplies drowned the marketplace.
Adding to the downward pressure at Sumas were significantly softer California prices. At Topock, the southern California border, prices slumped into the $3.50s, down nearly 30 cents from Wednesday.
At Niagara, the eastern Canadian export point, prices fell by about 25 cents to the $3.70s per mmBtu.
Sources said the sell-off in the futures market was the major factor contributing to lower Niagara prices.
February Henry Hub natgas dove to a low of $3.25 in Thursday's session, down 26.3 cents from Wednesday's settlement.
